basal insulin provides a continuous low level of insulin, and prandial insulin covers the increase in glucose with a meal. Prandial
insulin may be given at prespeciﬁed doses (for example, 5 units with each meal) or be based on carbohydrate intake. In addition,
patients may administer correctional insulin: rapid acting insulin given to cover high glucose levels, typically per a sliding scale
(Table 8). Patients with type 1 diabetes typically will use all three of these types of insulin, for example 15 units of long-acting
(basal) insulin at bedtime, and with each meal 1 unit of rapid acting (prandial) insulin per 15 g of carbohydrate plus an additional
1 unit of rapid acting (correctional) insulin for every 30 mg/dL blood glucose above 120 mg/dL. Alternatively, they may use an
